title: The finish contract
intro: Choose a situation and see whether the outcome is accepted or refused, and for which reasons. Every scenario here is executed against the real binary by test/cases/34_command_fixtures.sh, so this page cannot claim behaviour the tool does not have.

scenarios.title: Nothing in place yet
scenarios.explain: Two contract lines are unmet and both are named at once. A worker who fixes one and is refused again for the next learns the contract one round trip at a time, so every cause is reported together.

scenarios.title: Work outside the claimed scope
scenarios.explain: The task claimed lib. A change under docs is work the task did not claim, and it is refused whatever else is in place.

scenarios.title: An unresolved question is open
scenarios.explain: An open question refuses completed, and only completed. The same task can be finished as blocked, which is the honest outcome when the answer is not yours to give.

scenarios.title: The verification command runs and fails
scenarios.explain: The command is run, not asserted. Its exit code and duration are recorded whatever it returns, so "verification ran" cannot be claimed without something having actually run.

scenarios.title: finish --check with no active task
scenarios.explain: This is why a pre-push hook can run finish --check unconditionally: a repository with no active task is not a failing repository.

scenarios.title: Everything in place
scenarios.explain: Accepted, and the ledger records the outcome together with the verification that earned it.
